english.title: Employer / self-employed person fail to discharge general health / safety duty to person other than employee

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being

(A)_[an employer, failed to conduct your undertaking in such a way to ensure, so far as was reasonably practicable, that persons not in your employment]_
(B)_[a self-employed person who conducted an undertaking of a prescribed description, failed to conduct your undertaking in such a way to ensure, so far as was reasonably practicable, that you and other persons (not being your employees)]_

who may have been affected thereby, were not exposed to risks to their health and safety
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 3 and 33(1)(a) of, and Schedule 3A to, the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
employer failed to
discharge duty so far as reasonably practicable
to conduct his undertaking in such a way as to ensure
persons not in his employment were not exposed to risks to
their health and safety
OR
self-employed person failed to
discharge duty so far as reasonably practicable
to conduct his undertaking in such a way as to ensure
that he and other persons not being his employees were not exposed to risks to
their health and safety

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Proceedings for an offence shall not, in England and Wales, be instituted except by an inspector or the Environment Agency or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions, see section 38 of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.

consent.description: Health and Safety at Work Inspectorate

other.penalty:
Either way -
Summary: 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2002; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see Schedule 3A to the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
